Senses.Explanation: The black dragon is the dragon beneath whose jaw the records place a brilliant pearl. In the Complete Book of the Five Lamps, Tianyi Yihuai's awakening verse speaks of seizing that pearl, and his final verse says that the dragon's horn is crushed. In the Compendium of the Five Lamps, an unnamed monk asks Dapu Xuantong how the pearl can be obtained; Dapu answers by clapping and looking sharply. Yu'an Yu later uses the black dragon's chin-pearl image while appraising the Nanyuan cat case. Wuyi Yuanlai's Extensive Record warns of mortal danger, while the Recorded Sayings of Sanyi Mingyu announces the pearl in hand. The Song of the Black Dragon's Pearl in the Zutang Collection is Danxia Tianran's named composition; it develops the pearl phrase but does not change the headword from the dragon into the pearl. Thus the dragon, its jaw, horn, and guarded pearl form one referential family, while the actions performed around them are deployments rather than extra senses. The headword occurs 364 times in 152 allowlist texts.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide creature referent. The inherited pearl gloss is revised because the headword names the black dragon; the pearl under its jaw belongs to the recurrent phrase family.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Tianyi Yihuai: Tianyi Yihuai's awakening verse says that he seizes the bright pearl from beneath the black dragon's jaw.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。驪龍頷下珠如何取得。師乃拊掌瞬視。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Dapu Xuantong section: an unnamed monk asks how to obtain the pearl beneath the black dragon's chin; Dapu claps and looks. All six rungs leave the monk unnamed.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 僧問 introduces the black-dragon question; Dapu responds only by clapping and looking.

Occurrences.Kwic: 解驪龍頷下之珠。直須不顧危亡，到手始得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Wuyi Yuanlai (無異元來禪師廣錄), spoken by Wuyi Yuanlai: he says that taking the pearl requires disregarding mortal danger until it is in hand.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拍案一下云：「驪龍珠在手，何處不稱尊？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Sanyi Mingyu (三宜盂禪師語錄), spoken by Sanyi Mingyu: after striking the table he says that the black dragon's pearl is in hand. Sanyi Mingyu is not yet represented in the local roster.
